cases.title: Naturipe Farms and Hortifrut expand berry genetics platform with Mountain Blue

source_artifact.title: Naturipe Farms and Hortifrut expand berry genetics platform with Mountain Blue

segments.text: Joint Naturipe Farms and Hortifrut announcement dated 30 July 2026 of an expanded berry genetics platform reached through a strategic collaboration with Mountain Blue Orchards. Hortifrut states it gains access to new elite blueberry selections for the United States, Mexico, Peru and other Latin American countries. Hortifrut CEO Hector Lujan and Mountain Blue International Business Manager Mano Babiolakis are quoted. The release also mentions Hortifrut's 2025 global B Corp certification.

If it holds, this connects the largest listed blueberry producer to the Ridley breeding lineage, which until now reached the Americas through separate licensing arrangements. It is the single most consequential structural development in the package, and it rests on one originating announcement.

cases.title: Costa Group enters new ownership phase as experienced consortium takes control

source_artifact.title: Costa Group enters new ownership phase as experienced consortium takes control

segments.text: Costa's announcement of 26 February 2024 that a consortium of Paine Schwartz Partners, Driscoll's, Inc. and British Columbia Investment Management Corporation has taken control at A$3.20 per share, with Harry Debney as interim chief executive. The release notes the company's origins with the Costa family in Geelong, Victoria in the late 1800s and a history of more than 120 years, and states that Costa launched a record four new blueberry varieties during 2023.

Driscoll's, itself a blueberry breeder and licensor, becoming a part-owner of Costa, another blueberry breeder and licensor, links two breeding programmes through ownership rather than through a licence. That is a materially different kind of connection and is easy to miss if only licensing relationships are tracked.

source_artifact.title: Agrovision celebrates 10 years of bringing the world a better berry

segments.text: Agrovision's own release of 5 February 2024 states that the company was established in 2013, marks its tenth anniversary, reports more than US$350 million invested in operations over the previous six years, and describes itself as the third largest blueberry grower in Peru. It states that Agrovision partners with leading breeders to develop a broad portfolio of premium varietals, names Steve Magami as co-founder and executive chairman, and refers to the Big Skye brand in China.

The company's own wording, partners with leading breeders, is the clearest available statement that it accesses rather than owns genetics. Combined with the absence of any patent or plant breeders' right in its name, it settles the classification: licensee, not breeder.

cases.title: Driscoll's files appeal in strawberry patent case

source_artifact.title: Driscoll's files appeal in strawberry patent case

segments.text: Driscoll's announcement of a protective appeal, dated 14 May 2025, against summary judgment for California Berry Cultivars in the Eastern District of California. The release states that Driscoll's develops exclusive patented berry varieties, that because Driscoll's does not sell its plants there is no legitimate way for the defendant to have obtained the patented varieties, that it grows through more than 900 independent growers, and that its berries are grown in more than 20 countries and sold in more than 40 across North America, Australia, Europe and China. It names Soren Bjorn as chief executive.

The litigation itself concerns strawberry, not blueberry, and is recorded here only to prevent it being carried into blueberry analysis by mistake. The release is retained because it is the best available first-party statement of Driscoll's licensing model, grower network and geographic reach.

cases.title: Costa launches BluGenix with five blueberry varieties suited to Yunnan

source_artifact.title: Costa launches BluGenix with five blueberry varieties suited to Yunnan

segments.text: Reports the launch of BluGenix on 29 May 2026 as the brand and platform for Costa's blueberry breeding programme, introduced with five varieties: Bounty, Breeze, Cascade, Delight and Eterna. Shelf life of 27 days at 4 degrees Celsius is claimed for all five and up to 50 days for Eterna. Costa chief executive Marc Werner and Leon Van Biljon, regional director of Costa Berry International, are quoted. The article describes the programme as drawing on close to 40 years of plant breeding expertise, and names South Africa, Zimbabwe, Morocco, the United States, Mexico, Peru, China and Australia as growing countries for BluGenix varieties.

A competitor putting a brand in front of its breeding programme is a shift from selling varieties to selling a platform, which is the same move Fall Creek made with Sekoya and United Exports with OZblu. The shelf-life claims carry no method, and the close to 40 years figure contradicts the more than 25 years Costa states on its own programme page.

source_artifact.title: Agrovision Corp seeks year-round blueberry supply from Peru, Mexico and Morocco

segments.text: Reports that Agrovision's Peruvian operation began with the varieties Biloxi and Ventura and has since moved to other varieties, among which those of the Sekoya programme. Gives 2022 figures of 2,800 hectares of berries across Peru, Mexico and Morocco, turnover of US$210 million and more than 2,500 containers exported, 40 per cent to China. Names Peruvian operations at Olmos and Morrope in Lambayeque, Mexican operations in Jalisco above 300 hectares and Moroccan operations in Souss-Massa at 250 hectares.

Names the specific genetics Agrovision relies on. A grower of this scale moving from public varieties onto a club platform is exactly the kind of demand-side shift that determines whether a managed-variety platform succeeds.

cases.title: Blueberry spat continues with war of words

source_artifact.title: Blueberry spat continues with war of words

segments.text: Report by Mike Knowles on a dispute between United Exports and the Rossouw Group's Ross Berries operation, in which two containers of about 27 tonnes were seized in Rotterdam on 27 October and 5 November 2020. United Exports asserted plant breeders' rights ownership in South Africa and the European Union and announced a five-year South African investment plan of R1.3 billion, about US$85 million.

cases.title: Plant Breeders' Rights record - Sekoya Grande

source_artifact.title: Plant Breeders' Rights record - Sekoya Grande

segments.text: Canadian plant breeders' rights record for 'FC13-122'. Application 18-9614 dated 2018-09-20, granted 2023-10-06, certificate 6925, expiring 2043-10-06. Breeders Peter Stefan Boches, Haley Belnap-McCall and Adam L. Wagner. Parentage 'ZF06-050' x 'ZF06-013' made in 2010 at Lowell, Oregon and selected in 2013. The examiner description records very strong vigour, large fruit, very firm fruit, high sweetness and high acidity, observed in a 2022 Chilliwack, British Columbia trial laid out as a randomised complete block with four replicates of three plants.

Canadian plant breeders' rights examination reports are among the very few publicly available descriptions of a blueberry cultivar that are produced by an independent examiner from a replicated comparative trial with a named location and season. They are therefore the strongest available counterweight to owner trait claims, even though the descriptors are ordinal rather than numeric.
